description: Pushing to a protected branch (master, production-*) is the operator's call, like a merge. Feature branches and PRs are not.
_on_error_why: Fails closed, like bitbucket-merge: a push to master or a production branch lands on the shared branch and is not undone by the agent that did it, while a refused command costs one retry.
_match_why: A DENY, not an ask and not grantable (HAG-50, Gary 2026-09-29): the operator pushes to these branches, full stop. The protected set is the day job's, master and production-<anything>; edit the two names in the pattern for another floor (main and release/* are NOT in it). Judged per PARSED command, so wrappers (bash -c, sh -c, env, sudo, cd x &&, an absolute path, git -C/-c/--git-dir) arrive as the bare invocation. DENIED: git push, git subtree push and git send-pack whose DESTINATION is protected - a bare name after the remote (git push origin master), the right side of a refspec (HEAD:master, feat:refs/heads/production-x), a forced refspec (+master), a delete (:master, --delete/-d origin master), any of those with --force/--force-with-lease, and the pushes that reach every branch at once (--all, --branches, --mirror, and a wildcard refspec such as refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*). ALLOWED: a feature-branch push, forced or not; a protected branch as the SOURCE only (master:feat/x); names that merely contain the word (feat/master, masterclass, fix/production-notes, bare production); a tag; a remote that happens to be named production-*; --dry-run or -n (only as a whole word that is not a flag's value, so git push -o --dry-run origin master is still denied); bb pr create with a protected destination, which is how the work should reach it. The first word after push is taken as the remote, as git does, so git push master names a remote, not a branch. Names are case-sensitive, as Bitbucket's are. NOT COVERED: (1) a push that names no destination - bare git push, git push origin, git push origin HEAD - which goes where the current branch and push.default say; the push_destination card resolves it, and until then it is only asked about under remote-push; (2) a destination set in git config (remote.<name>.push); (3) an alias (git pm) or a script file that pushes; (4) a push option whose quoted text contains the word, e.g. -o 'why not master', is denied because the parsed form loses the quotes (a false deny, one retry). Place this rule BEFORE remote-push: rules are first-match.
reason: That push goes to a protected branch (master or production-*), which is the operator's call. Push a feature branch and open a PR with bb pr create instead, report the PR link, and say it is ready to merge.
